note: Component-construction standards for the Baltor Context Engine. Each standard is a normative description of how the repo ACTUALLY builds one of the canonical 25 component patterns, derived from real exemplar modules. A standard is the contract a template generates against and a check enforces. Do not hand-type counts or model dimensions here (No-Magic-Values); cite real repo paths in 'examples'. status_enum gates how strictly a standard is enforced.

standards.title: Governed source adapter behind one SourceAdapterPort
standards.applies_to: Any module that ingests an external source type (api/structured-record, csv, json/webhook, feed) and normalizes it into governed artifacts.
must_have: implements the structural SourceAdapter Protocol (source_type, parser_provider, ingest(...))
normalizes every source into the SAME governed artifact chain (source_record -> source_field -> atomic_fact / narrative_allegation)
content-addressed ids and content_hash (hashlib over sorted-key JSON); same payload -> same artifacts
carries tenant_id + scope + source_id + lineage (parent_artifact_id) on every artifact
structured official fields are promotion_eligible facts; free-text becomes held-out unverified allegations
a source whose parser is unavailable returns an explicit NON-CONSUMABLE reason + stored raw artifact, never a fabricated result
must_not_have: no wall-clock in ids/content (no datetime.now/time.time)
no network call at import time
no raw source promoted directly to truth
no third-party SDK reached as a global; go through ports
standards.naming_rules: Module file is the source family name (sanctions_feed_live, ecfr_feed); source_type is a lowercase token registered in contract_registry.json#source_types.
standards.file_location_rules: scripts/ingest/<source_family>.py (the adapter). Shared adapter Protocol + helpers stay in scripts/ingest/source_adapters.py.
standards.contract_rules: Emits source_record + source_field + atomic_fact + narrative_allegation artifact_types (registered in contract_registry.json#artifact_types). Consumes a FetchRequest-style input contract.
standards.proof_rules: A check_*.py proves: determinism (same payload -> same ids), narrative vs structured split, NON-CONSUMABLE boundary, tenant/scope present. Offline + --self-test + PASS/FAIL + exit 0/1.
standards.doc_rules: A docs section page covers Purpose/Inputs/Outputs/Contracts/Adapters/Proofs with the required headings.
standards.registry_rules: Register source_type in contract_registry.json#source_types; register adapter under a section_maturity_matrix.json section (category ingestion); register any new artifact_type.
standards.security_rules: No real PII/secrets in fixtures; free-text held-out; no secret markers in emitted artifacts.
standards.observability_rules: Emit a durable source ingestion event onto the ONE event log; structured fields, no PII.

standards.title: Idempotent ingestion sync / fetch loop
standards.applies_to: Modules that fetch a source on a cadence (or on demand) and stage source_records without re-ingesting duplicates.
must_have: content-addressed snapshot hash so a re-fetch of identical content is a no-op
idempotency guard (mark_processed style) so a duplicate snapshot does not re-stage
explicit NON-CONSUMABLE handling when the source/parser is unavailable
injected clock for any timestamp in staged records (no wall-clock in identity)
must_not_have: no network at import time
no fabricated rows when a fetch fails
no second durable store / queue framework
standards.contract_rules: Produces source_record artifacts; consumes a FetchRequest. Reuses scripts/durable_store.py for staging + idempotency.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts idempotency (re-run -> 0 new rows) and NON-CONSUMABLE boundary, offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Section page documents cadence, snapshot identity, and the non-consumable boundary.
standards.registry_rules: Register the queue_name (if any) in contract_registry.json#queue_names and the section in section_maturity_matrix.json.
standards.security_rules: Public metadata only; never store credentials in staged records.
standards.observability_rules: Emit a durable ingest/sync event; counts only, no payload PII.

standards.title: Durable CommandEnvelope enqueued onto one durable store
standards.applies_to: Any unit of work submitted for asynchronous, retryable, exactly-once-effect processing.
must_have: a CommandEnvelope-shaped payload with command_type + identity fields
enqueued via scripts/durable_store.py (one durable store, SQLite-backed) with an idempotency_key
max_attempts / lease semantics so retries -> DLQ, never infinite
permanent vs retryable failure distinction (PermanentJobError -> immediate DLQ)
must_not_have: no second queue/bus/worker framework
no wall-clock in idempotency_key derivation
no direct side effects outside the handler contract
standards.naming_rules: command_type is a dotted token (pipeline.run_step, context.consume) registered in contract_registry.json#command_types.
standards.file_location_rules: Command producers live with their domain; the durable contract is scripts/durable_store.py.
standards.contract_rules: command_type registered in contract_registry.json#command_types; handler verdict drives ack/nack.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts idempotency_key dedupe + DLQ on permanent failure, offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document command_type, payload shape, idempotency key, retry/DLQ behavior.
standards.security_rules: No secrets in payloads; tenant_id carried for isolation.
standards.observability_rules: Emit a durable event on enqueue/complete/fail.

standards.title: Stateless durable worker claim/ack loop
standards.applies_to: A standalone worker process that pulls jobs from the durable queue, runs a handler, and ack/nacks.
must_have: stateless claim-loop: claim (lease) -> handler(store, job) -> ack/nack
N workers against one queue share work with NO double-processing (BEGIN IMMEDIATE + busy_timeout serialize claims across processes)
backoff when idle + exit after K empty polls so a drain terminates
handler contract handler(store, job) -> result; raise to nack -> retry -> DLQ
default handler idempotent (records doc_id once; double-process detectable)
must_not_have: no shared in-process state assumed between workers
no second worker framework
no infinite run without a drain/exit condition
no wall-clock in job identity
standards.naming_rules: Worker module *_worker.py; worker_id is caller-supplied; queue is a registered queue_name.
standards.file_location_rules: scripts/ (top-level worker) or scripts/context_workers/ for the worker fleet.
standards.contract_rules: Reuses DurableStore claim/ack/lease/DLQ contract; routes by command_type.
standards.proof_rules: Proof: run >1 worker against one queue, assert each job processed exactly once + DLQ after max_attempts. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the claim/ack/lease/DLQ contract and the no-double-process guarantee.
standards.registry_rules: Register queue_name; register the section (category runtime) in section_maturity_matrix.json.
standards.security_rules: Tenant scope carried through; no secrets logged.
standards.observability_rules: Structured claim/ack/nack/dlq log events; durable Work-plane events.

standards.title: Processor run through the standard ProcessorHarness via the registry
standards.applies_to: Any pipeline step that transforms artifacts; invoked only through the harness + registry, never directly.
must_have: processor reaches the outside world ONLY through RuntimeContext ports (never globals/SDKs/the admin bus)
registered in scripts/runtime/processor_registry.py and run via run_command(registry, command, ctx)
harness verdict {ok, retryable, error|result} drives ack/nack
deterministic: same inputs -> same artifacts; ids content-addressed; time injected
must_not_have: no direct global state / SDK import inside the processor body
no second harness or registry
no wall-clock in artifact identity
standards.naming_rules: processor_id is a dotted token registered in contract_registry.json#processor_ids.
standards.contract_rules: Consumes a CommandEnvelope; emits artifact_types; verdict shape stable.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts the processor runs through run_command and the verdict shape + determinism. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document processor_id, inputs, outputs, ports used.
standards.security_rules: Ports only; tenant isolation enforced via context.
standards.observability_rules: Emit step.completed / processor.failed events; structured logging via LoggerPort.

standards.title: Provider adapter behind a structural capability port
standards.applies_to: An adapter that fronts an external capability (model/gateway/object-store/secrets) behind a Protocol port.
must_have: satisfies a structural Protocol from scripts/runtime/ports.py (duck-typed; runtime_checkable)
swappable: an in-memory test adapter and a production adapter satisfy the SAME port
no secret literals; secrets resolved through SecretsResolverPort by ref
deterministic in tests (no live network in --self-test)
must_not_have: no global SDK reach from processors
no hard-coded api keys / endpoints in source
no second LLM gateway
standards.file_location_rules: Port Protocols in scripts/runtime/ports.py; capability catalog entries in catalog/adapters/<id>.yaml.
standards.contract_rules: Adapter conforms to a named Port; capability registered in external_capability_catalog.json.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts the adapter satisfies its Port (isinstance against runtime_checkable Protocol) and is swappable. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the port, the swap points, and the secret-ref contract.
standards.security_rules: Secrets by ref only; no key literals; user has accepted key-exposure risk policy but fixtures still carry none.
standards.observability_rules: Structured call/latency/error logs through LoggerPort; no payload secrets.

standards.title: Projection-only HTTP route via a pure request handler
standards.applies_to: Any HTTP route that exposes engine output; must be projection-only and testable without a socket.
must_have: pure handler (method, path, body) -> (status, json) so the contract is testable WITHOUT a socket
NEVER fabricates truth: calls the proven engine and returns its contract object
projection_only: reads/returns; computes no truth, bypasses no gate
no secret markers ever emitted in a response
must_not_have: no business logic / truth computation in the handler
no direct DB writes from a GET
no secret/credential leakage in responses
standards.naming_rules: Route 'METHOD /api/<area>/<resource>'; handler module scripts/api_<area>_handler.py exporting ROUTES.
standards.file_location_rules: scripts/api_<area>_handler.py; the admin server delegates to it (MAIN wires the server).
standards.contract_rules: Returns a registered contract (e.g. ContextResponse); route registered in contract_registry.json#api_routes with projection_only:true and an owner.
standards.proof_rules: Proof drives the handler directly (no socket), asserts status + contract shape + no secret markers. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document route, method, returns-contract, projection-only guarantee, owner.
standards.registry_rules: Register the route in contract_registry.json#api_routes; MAIN folds into section_maturity_matrix.json.
standards.security_rules: Token-gate mutations; deny secret markers; projection-only.
standards.observability_rules: Structured request log (route, status); no body PII.

standards.title: Projection-only UI page that renders an API (computes no truth)
standards.applies_to: Any web page that displays engine output by fetching a projection API.
must_have: the page fetches a projection API and RENDERS only (no truth computed, stored, or mutated client-side)
explicit comment marking it projection-only
no secrets / tokens hard-coded in the page
held-out items shown SEPARATELY from served truth
must_not_have: no client-side truth computation
no embedded credentials
no direct DB / engine access from the browser
standards.contract_rules: Consumes a registered api_route projection; renders its contract fields.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts the page references only projection endpoints + carries the projection-only marker + no secret literal. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document which API the page projects and the projection-only guarantee.
standards.registry_rules: Register the ui page under its section (MAIN folds into section_maturity_matrix.json#ui_pages).
standards.security_rules: No tokens/secrets in the page; gating happens at the API.
standards.observability_rules: n/a client-side beyond fetch status display.

standards.title: Deterministic offline proof script with --self-test
standards.applies_to: Every check_*.py / proof that asserts a contract holds.
must_have: --self-test mode that prints '[ok]/[FAIL] <name>' lines and a clear PASS/FAIL summary
exit 0 on pass, 1 on fail (return code drives the flywheel)
deterministic + offline: tempfile.mkdtemp for any fs, content-addressed ids, no wall-clock, no RNG, no network
cleans up its temp dir
asserts against REAL repo artifacts where it claims to (no fabricated numbers)
must_not_have: no network call
no datetime.now/time.time/random in assertions
no leftover temp files
no fabricated 'detected' counts
standards.naming_rules: scripts/check_<thing>.py; a local check(name, ok, detail) helper.
standards.file_location_rules: scripts/ (proofs) or alongside the module under scripts/<area>/.
standards.proof_rules: Self-referential: the script IS the proof; CLI parses --self-test and returns its int.
standards.doc_rules: Module docstring states what unit + integration it proves and the CLI.
standards.registry_rules: MAIN registers the proof in scripts/baltor_flywheel.py PROOF_MODULES as (path, label).
standards.security_rules: No real PII/secrets in fixtures or logs.
standards.observability_rules: PASS/FAIL lines are the observable surface.

standards.title: Section documentation page with the required headings
standards.applies_to: Every component/section doc page that prevents repeated slow or incorrect paths.
must_have: the required headings: Purpose, Owner, Inputs, Outputs, Contracts, Ports, Adapters, Registry entries, Proofs, Commands, Limitations, Opportunities, Next steps
real owner path + real proof paths cited
product vocabulary (Knowledge Corpus / If Statement / Action; component/subcomponent; avoid 'artifact'/'manifest' in new prose except quoting schemas)
must_not_have: no missing required heading
no hand-typed counts that can drift (No-Magic-Values)
no fabricated file paths
standards.contract_rules: Lists the input/output contracts the section uses.
standards.proof_rules: A docs-coverage check asserts the required headings exist.
standards.registry_rules: MAIN links the doc under section_maturity_matrix.json#docs.

standards.title: Versioned contract schema validated by ref
standards.applies_to: Any data contract exchanged between components (request/response/artifact envelope).
must_have: schema_version field on the object (e.g. ContextResponse)
validated through scripts/runtime/schema_validator.validate_ref(obj, ref)
version lives in the schema_version field, NEVER in the id or name
registered in contract_registry.json (artifact_types / api_routes returns)
must_not_have: no version baked into ids/names
no unvalidated contract crossing a component boundary
no silent schema drift (a change is a new .vN)
standards.file_location_rules: Schemas under schemas/ or the runtime; validator scripts/runtime/schema_validator.py.
standards.contract_rules: Self-referential; this IS the contract standard.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts validate_ref accepts a good object and rejects a malformed one. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the contract fields + version policy.
standards.observability_rules: Validation failures surfaced as errors, not swallowed.

standards.title: Content-addressed governed artifact object
standards.applies_to: Every governed object emitted by the engine (source_record, atomic_fact, narrative_allegation, receipts).
must_have: artifact_type from the registered set + content_hash (hashlib over sorted-key JSON)
tenant_id + scope + source lineage (parent_artifact_id, source_handle)
claim_status + promotion_eligible flags (facts eligible; allegations held-out)
id derived from content, not wall-clock
must_not_have: no PII in artifact bodies (synthetic/public only)
no wall-clock in artifact id
no truncation-only ids (stable hash suffix required)
standards.file_location_rules: Emitted by ingest/runtime modules; type registry architecture/contract_registry.json#artifact_types.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts content-addressing (same body -> same id) + required security metadata. Offline, --self-test.
standards.security_rules: Security metadata (tenant/scope/claim_status) required; no secret markers.
standards.observability_rules: Emit on creation via the event log.

standards.title: Governed optimization candidate with baseline/regression/promotion
standards.applies_to: Any optimizer that proposes a reduced/improved context pack.
must_have: optimizer satisfies the stable Optimizer port (optimize(pack, signals) -> pack); chainable
candidate measured against a BaselineSnapshot for lift
a RegressionGate (no answer-fact loss, source handles preserved, no held-out/allegation promoted, no tenant leak, nothing fabricated)
PROMOTE only on measured lift + zero regressions; emit content-addressed OptimizationReceipt
must_not_have: no silent speedup without measured lift
no held-out item re-entering the promoted pack
no second optimizer framework
no wall-clock in receipt id
standards.contract_rules: Consumes only gate-allow artifacts; emits OptimizationReceipt.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts promotion only on lift + zero regression and that a held-out item cannot be promoted. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the optimizer port + regression gate + receipt.
standards.registry_rules: Register the optimization section in section_maturity_matrix.json.
standards.security_rules: No tenant leak across optimization; held-out never promoted.

standards.title: Deterministic reconciliation decision over conflicting claims
standards.applies_to: Any module that resolves conflicting claims across sources into a decision.
must_have: deterministic decision given the same conflicting inputs (no RNG)
decision records the winning claim + reason + the losers (audit lineage)
authority/recency rules explicit, not implicit
decision id content-addressed
must_not_have: no nondeterministic tie-break
no silent drop of the losing claim (must be recorded)
no wall-clock in decision id
standards.naming_rules: ReconciliationDecision object; reason an explicit code.
standards.contract_rules: Consumes conflicting atomic_facts; emits a reconciliation decision artifact.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts determinism + the loser is recorded with a reason. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the authority/recency rules + decision shape.
standards.registry_rules: Register the reconciliation section in section_maturity_matrix.json.

standards.title: Watchtower verification task enforcing minimum freshness
standards.applies_to: Background verification tasks that re-check fragile/volatile facts for freshness.
must_have: a freshness bound: a fragile fact past its minimum freshness must NOT be served as truth
deterministic given injected clock (freshness compared to an injected 'now', not wall-clock)
stale fact -> held-out / re-verify, never silently served
task is a durable command (reuses the worker/command pattern)
must_not_have: no wall-clock comparison in the proof
no serving of a stale fragile fact
no second scheduler framework
standards.naming_rules: Watchtower task command_type dotted token; freshness bound a named constant.
standards.file_location_rules: scripts/context_workers/ (the worker fleet) + the consumption gate.
standards.contract_rules: Consumes atomic_facts with a fragility/freshness signal; emits a verification task + held-out warning.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts a stale fact is held out given an injected now. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the freshness bound + the held-out behavior.
standards.registry_rules: Register the watchtower section in section_maturity_matrix.json.

standards.title: Tenant isolation carried on every governed object and boundary
standards.applies_to: Every component that touches per-tenant data (ingest, runtime, consumption, API).
must_have: tenant_id + scope on every artifact and command
no cross-tenant private fact served as truth (scope global_public vs tenant)
the API/consumption layer filters by tenant_id before serving
experiments / candidate rows isolated from active tenant-visible data
must_not_have: no global mutable state mixing tenants
no tenant_id defaulted-away on a write path
no cross-tenant leak through optimization/consumption
standards.naming_rules: tenant_id field name is exactly tenant_id; scope token is global_public or tenant.
standards.contract_rules: tenant_id required on requests/artifacts; scope governs promotion eligibility.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts tenant A cannot see tenant B's private fact through the served response. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the tenant/scope model + the isolation boundary.
standards.observability_rules: Tenant id in structured logs (not PII).

standards.title: Review pack / queue for high-risk artifacts before promotion
standards.applies_to: Any flow that routes high-risk or open-review artifacts to a human review queue before tenant-visible promotion.
must_have: a review ticket opened when risk warrants (the review_ticket row family)
an artifact with open review tickets is NOT tenant-visible (promotion boundary)
deterministic review pack content-addressed (no wall-clock in id)
explicit risk reasons recorded on the pack
must_not_have: no promotion of an artifact with open review tickets
no silent auto-approve of high-risk artifacts
no wall-clock in pack id
standards.naming_rules: Review pack object; review_ticket row family.
standards.contract_rules: Consumes flagged artifacts; emits a review pack + review_ticket rows.
standards.proof_rules: Proof asserts an artifact with an open ticket cannot be promoted. Offline, --self-test.
standards.doc_rules: Document the review-pack shape + the promotion boundary.
standards.registry_rules: Register the review section in section_maturity_matrix.json.
standards.security_rules: High-risk artifacts gated behind review; no PII in the pack.
